subject: microbiology
title: Streptolysin O, ASO Titres and Rheumatic Fever Serology

steps.tx: **Streptolysin O** is pyogenes' oxygen labile, cholesterol binding cytolysin (inactive when oxidised, restored by reducing agents), haemolysing red cells subsurface in agar stabs and killing leukocytes, strongly immunogenic, so its antibody (ASO) becomes the retrospective infection marker. Streptolysin S, oxygen stable and surface carried, makes the surface beta zone and is not antigenic.
steps.say: O hides from oxygen and advertises to antibody; S works the surface silently.

left.title: Streptolysin O
points: Subsurface haemolysis in stabs and anaerobic incubation

right.title: Streptolysin S
points: Surface beta haemolysis on aerobic plates

steps.tx: **Streptolysin O** is the oxygen labile, cholesterol binding cytolysin of Streptococcus pyogenes. Oxidised toxin is inactive and reducing agents restore it, so red cells lyse along a subsurface agar stab while leukocytes are also killed. The toxin is strongly immunogenic, and antistreptolysin O antibody becomes the retrospective marker of recent infection. Streptolysin S is oxygen stable, rides on the surface, makes the visible beta zone, and does not raise antibody.
steps.say: Oxygen labile streptolysin O lyses red cells only under the agar surface and raises antistreptolysin O antibody after infection. Oxygen stable streptolysin S makes the surface beta zone and is not antigenic.

vis.alt: A blood agar plate shows a stab track with haemolysis beneath the surface while the surface growth has little clearing.
vis.caption: A blood agar stab shows clearing of red cells along the deep track, with little surface zone. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The **ASO titre** (antistreptolysin O) rises one to three weeks after pyogenes infection, peaks around three to five, and fades over months, upper limits varying by age and geography (200 to 300 Todd units traditions), a single high or rising paired titre supporting recent infection in rheumatic fever and glomerulonephritis workups, never diagnosing active infection alone.
steps.say: ASO is last month's streptococcus in numbers; it supports sequelae, not sore throats.

left.title: ASO kinetics
points: Rise 1 to 3 weeks, peak 3 to 5 weeks
Skin infection raises ASO poorly (cholesterol in skin binds SLO)
Upper limits age and region adjusted

right.title: Partner antibodies
points: Anti DNase B: better after skin infection, GN workhorse
Two antibodies raise sensitivity in sequelae panels

steps.tx: **Rheumatic fever** follows pharyngitis after a latent two to three weeks: immune cross reaction (M protein and streptococcal antigens against heart valve, myocardium, joints, brain basal ganglia, skin) producing Jones criteria carditis, migratory polyarthritis, chorea, erythema marginatum and nodules, with ASO or anti DNase B evidencing the antecedent infection.
steps.say: Two weeks after the throat, antibodies attack heart and joints by mistaken identity.

right.title: Evidence stack
points: ASO or anti DNase B elevation
Raised ESR and CRP (minors with fever, arthralgia)
Prior rheumatic history changes criteria (recurrence pathways)

steps.tx: **Molecular mimicry** mechanises rheumatic fever: antibodies and T cells against streptococcal M and carbohydrate epitopes cross react with valve myosin, tropomyosin and laminin, valve endothelium upregulates adhesion, and recurrent episodes scar valves toward rheumatic heart disease, prevented by penicillin prophylaxis adherence, the module's most consequential prescription.
steps.say: Prevent the next streptococcal throat and the valve stops accumulating scars.

nodes.label: Group A pharyngitis in susceptible host
Cross reactive antibodies and T cells form

steps.tx: **Secondary prophylaxis** after rheumatic fever is benzathine penicillin G injections every three to four weeks for years graded by carditis severity (without carditis five years or to 21, with carditis longer, residual valve disease longest), allergy alternatives macrolide, adherence systems (registers, recall, pain mitigation) deciding its real effectiveness in endemic programmes.
steps.say: Monthly benzathine for years is valve insurance; registers and recall pay the premiums.

left.title: Duration grammar
points: No carditis: 5 years or age 21, longer greater
Residual valve disease: 10 years or 40, sometimes life

right.title: Adherence machinery
points: Oral penicillin twice daily less reliable fallback

steps.tx: **ASO false trails** include liver disease and hyperlipidaemia falsely elevating, early antibiotics blunting rises, immunodeficiency silencing, and healthy schoolchildren carrying high baselines in endemic regions, which is why cut offs are population percentiles (80th) and trends outrank single results in every guideline.
steps.say: Endemic children run high ASO at baseline; trends and partners beat single numbers.

left.title: False highs and lows
points: Skin infection: ASO low, anti DNase B answers

right.title: Sequelae panels
points: Order ASO plus anti DNase B together
Throat culture often negative by sequelae time
Echo finds subclinical carditis modern criteria

steps.tx: **Streptolysin O in the laboratory** still works: ASO measured by latex agglutination or nephelometry standardised in IU, Todd unit heritage, with quality systems less romantic than the toxin itself. The assay's longevity (1930s principle) beside MALDI benches marks serology's two speeds in one laboratory.
steps.say: A 1930s toxin antibody measured by nephelometry still decides rheumatic workups.

left.title: Assay forms
points: Paired sera in same run ideally

right.title: Ordering wisdom
points: For rheumatic fever and GN evidence

steps.tx: **Other streptococcal antibodies** (anti DNase B foremost) share this lesson because sequelae clinics order them together: anti DNase B peaks later (six to eight weeks) and answers skin infection where ASO fails, together lifting evidence sensitivity above 90 percent after true infections when both are measured.
steps.say: Order both antibodies; skin infections answer DNase B while throats answer both.

left.title: Anti DNase B
points: Rises after skin and throat infection

right.title: Panel interpretation
points: Both negative: argues against recent pyogenes
Culture and clinical criteria complete Jones
